summary: This corrective fix genuinely closes the cross-tenant privilege-escalation bug found in PR #561's original audit: getPromptLifecycleRule() and checkPromptEvalBudget() were re-implemented to take no orgId parameter and read only the scope_type='platform' module_rule_configs row, and I verified in module-rule-service.ts that setModuleRule()'s WRITABLE_SCOPE_TYPES set ('org'/'project'/'client') genuinely excludes 'platform', so this is a real structural floor rather than a role check that could itself be routed around; a grep confirmed no remaining call site in prompt-governance-service.ts/prompt-os-service.ts/prompt-eval-service.ts still threads an orgId into these two functions. The PII credit-card regex was correctly tightened to a real Luhn checksum (bounded, non-catastrophic regex, no ReDoS concern) with tests proving both the true-positive (Visa test PAN) and the false-positive case it removes. The new prompt-governance-gates.test.ts adds real DB-mocked coverage of the previously-untested runLifecycleTransitionGates/checkPromptEvalBudget, including two regression tests that directly reproduce the audited exploit scenario and would fail under the old org-parameterized code. The residual architectural limitation (checkPromptPolicyDeny's org-scoped ABAC evaluated against a platform-wide resource, causing org-to-org asymmetric strictness) is honestly documented and I confirmed abac-policy-service.ts is genuinely deny-only with no 'allow' effect anywhere, so that asymmetry can only over-restrict, never re-open the escalation this PR fixes -- deferring a full platform-scope ABAC capability is a reasonable scope boundary, not a swept-under-the-rug gap. Since this diff touches drizzle/*.sql, schema.ts, and permission-service.ts, it correctly falls under tier2 and must hold for human sign-off regardless of this approval.
